title: Clear words and an uncertain closeness

captions.physics: Clarifying a chosen condition’s actual meaning
captions.emotions: Feeling ambiguity in a boundary heard

meaning: You can state conversational terms openly and clarify an uncertain feeling separately, without treating an impression of a boundary as established knowledge of closeness.
text: A clearly named boundary can leave an unclear feeling. Justice in the physical position of Vishuddha clarifies a chosen condition’s actual meaning. The Sun in energy supports open, respectful expression of a wish. The Moon in emotions retains ambiguity in what is heard. Both the answer and its nuance can be discussed while remaining distinct. Honest words support what is actually known, and an impression can receive its own question instead of explaining the entire connection through one unfamiliar brief phrase.

For example, among acquaintances someone says, “I don’t want to discuss this here”. One hears a request for another place; the other thinks the subject is unwanted altogether. **An open boundary allows clarification of a personal impression.** Actual meaning and a continuation can be discussed. The condition need require neither immediate public discussion nor silent abandonment. Feeling can have words beyond concealing it or establishing a hidden refusal to listen.

The difficulty is eliminating every ambiguous nuance through stricter terms. Wording must prevent all possible guesses and conversation grows heavy. Asking about substance preserves proportion. An uncertain personal feeling deserves attention without continually enlarging promised explanations or making a personal answer an examination in flawless persuasion and identical reception.
